## 7. THE NEGATIVES

**These protect the product.** Every one of them is a place where the machinery was pointed at the project's own favourite hypothesis and the hypothesis lost. **Selectively reporting only the confirmatory results would void the differentiator.** None of these may ever be deleted from this file.

### 7.1 Flat 40-cell CAS detection collapses to chance under leakage control — `FALSIFY` at fixture level

Once the surface giveaways are removed from the prompts, a probe on hidden states lands at chance, and **shuffled labels do about as well as real ones**.

- Condition-3 (`n=1440`, chance **2.5%**): CAS hidden **6.53%** vs its own text baseline **6.25%** (lift **+0.28 pp** against a **+20 pp** gate); scrambled-CAS null **3.47%**.
- dual_labeled 40E marker-balanced fixture (`n=1000`, chance 2.5%): CAS hidden **5.5%** (best layer 20) vs CAS text **1.5%** (lift **+4.0 pp**) — and **scrambled-label null 5.0%**, statistically indistinguishable from the real result.
- F28 axis (`n=700`, chance **3.57%**): CAS recovered **3.57% — exactly the chance floor** — while the scrambled null recovered **6.43%**. **Shuffled labels beat real labels. That is the definitive no-signal signature.**
- Runner flag: `scrambled_cas_near_chance_no_clean_structure = failed`.

**Honest read:** marker-balanced fixtures over-correct — they strip the surface shortcut so hard that the model has no reason to internally represent the distinction, so there is no signal for a matched comparison to interpret. This is a fixture-design null as much as a CAS null. **But after Condition-3 (which passed eligibility and surface gates as ELIGIBLE/PASS and still returned 6.5%), the fixture-design excuse has largely run out.**

Artifacts: `docs/working/mtc_matched_taxonomy_20260530/condition3_mtc_comparator_result_20260531.json`; `RESULT_NOTE_20260531.md`; `surface_gate_condition3_result.json`. Model: GPT-NeoX-20B, 1440 items × 44 layers × 6144 dims, 720/720 split.

**Do not cite:** the "32% CAS text baseline" from the earlier capture runbook — it does **not** reproduce; the authoritative runner reports **1.5%** on the same npz.

### 7.2 Matched-Taxonomy Condition-3 — a rival taxonomy is ~13× more recoverable

On the **same rows and the same activations**: CAS 40-element hidden readout **0.0653**; the cardinality-matched non-CAS control (`topic_40 × frame_40`) scored hidden **0.8472** / text **0.9444**. Against a 28-class matched control: CAS **0.0655** (layer 42) vs NC28 hidden **0.8472**. A no-model lexical k-means-40 baseline scored **0.2264** — also ~**3.5×** CAS.

**This is the single most important mechanistic read in the project: the headline 95.6% 40E detection rode SURFACE/TOPIC structure.** The legacy spec sheet's own "necessary not sufficient" caveat was correct, and Condition-3 confirms it.

**Permanently untestable:** the original v1 95.625% fixture's specificity. Those activations were **lost with the prior pod** and cannot be re-probed.

### 7.3 Involution structure DISCONFIRMED — CAS's opposites are the LEAST opposite pairing available

CAS's sharpest geometric prediction is that `^2 Positive ↔ ^3 Negative`, `^5 Female ↔ ^6 Male`, `^8 Above/Cause ↔ ^9 Below/Effect` sit on opposite sides of representation space. Tested by an exact 15-matching permutation test per layer — is CAS's specific pairing of six operators more antipodal than the other 14 ways of pairing the same six?

- **CAS ranks 14/14 (LAST) on every one of the 43 real layers.** (Layer 0 = embeddings, degenerate.)
- Involution-pair centroid cosine is **POSITIVE** across all layers, **+0.32 to +0.61** (best-signal layers: L12 **+0.318**, L13 **+0.338**, L14 **+0.337**; L32 **+0.469**). **The pairs are similar, not opposite.**
- Involution pairs are also **less separable** than random pairs of the same six operators: L13 involution **0.7431** vs all-involved-pair **0.8449**; L12 **0.7269** vs **0.8347**; L32 **0.6667** vs **0.8264**. **Harder to tell apart, not oppositely placed.**

**Honest scope:** "antipodality about the global mean" is one operationalisation of opposition, and a finer subspace could still carry weak directional signal (the pairs *are* roughly 0.67-0.74 separable). **What is decisive is the relative result** — CAS's own pairing is the worst of fifteen on **every** real layer, a fair within-fixture comparison that kills "these are opposites in the model" as stated. Mechanistic read: the model groups `^2`/`^3` by shared topic and valence, not by CAS's claimed directional opposition.

Artifacts: `docs/working/gate2_closure/cas_specificity/RESULT_INVOLUTION_TEST_20260818.md`; `cas_involution_result.json`; `cas_involution_test.py`. Pure numpy on captured activations — no model or GPU, so nothing depends on inference-time randomness.

### 7.4 Domain precedence — PARTIAL, and plausibly generic

The one CAS relation that did **not** fail. P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O separation is real and the order holds — but the order CAS predicts is the same order a plain abstract-to-concrete gradient predicts, which every language model already carries.

- 4-way nearest-centroid held-out balanced accuracy climbs from **0.250** at the embedding layer (exactly chance) to **0.5165-0.5638 across layers 32-41**, then drops to **0.4501 at layer 42**. **This is the key contrast with the operator/involution collapse — the domain axis is real signal.** **Numbers corrected 2026-08-19:** the previous wording, *"0.52-0.56 in deep layers 32-42"*, excluded two of its own layers — `L35 = 0.51647513026651` sits below `0.52` and `L42 = 0.4501382188394754` sits well below the whole band. Exact `domain_sep4` values, `L32`→`L42`: `0.526927665254082`, `0.541678851836555`, `0.5466191907969111`, `0.51647513026651`, `0.5290198786853538`, `0.5377906316966481`, `0.5500028320718944`, `0.5523746382582272`, `0.5478589312727197`, `0.5637608036399963`, `0.4501382188394754`. (Error inherited verbatim from `RESULT_PRECEDENCE_TEST_20260818.md`; a correction note is appended there.)
- CAS's order is monotone on the descent axis on **43 of 44** layers; only the final layer 43 breaks it (to P-C-O-E).
- Strict "distance grows with order-gap" fit: CAS is in the **top-3 of 12** on **20 of 44** layers; at its best layer (32) `r = +0.597`, ranking **2/12** — **one non-CAS ordering fits slightly better even at CAS's best layer.** On layers **13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20** the fit **inverts to negative** (and again at layer **43**). **Range corrected 2026-08-19 from "13-18"** — the actual negative `cas_fit` layers in `cas_precedence_result.json` are `[13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 43]`, so the previous text **understated the inversion by two layers and omitted layer 43 entirely.** Same inherited-error note as above.

**The deflation is load-bearing:** finding four domain labels ordered along an abstract-to-concrete gradient is **expected with or without CAS**. Converting this into CAS-specificity requires a **matched non-CAS four-level abstractness taxonomy doing worse** on the same fixtures — an MTC-style control that has **not been run**. Until then this is **presence, not specificity**, and must not be reported as a CAS win.

Artifacts: `docs/working/gate2_closure/cas_specificity/RESULT_PRECEDENCE_TEST_20260818.md`; `cas_precedence_result.json`; `cas_precedence_test.py`. 360 rows per domain, balanced.

### 7.5 RPM prerequisite-chain geometry — NOT TESTABLE, not null

The Condition-3 captures carry **noetic, domain, and element labels only**. **0 RPM-labelled rows** across the 1440-item capture set. **Do not report this as a null or as evidence either way — it is an untested cell.** Reporting "RPM geometry not found" would be an overclaim. Separately, the owner-intended role of RPM is the steering-back mechanism (diagnose → localize → repair), which is a **live-model white-box task, not a static-capture detection test**.

### 7.6 Gate-2 independent scenario bank — REJECTED at G1

Four LLMs that had never seen CAS or TKS wrote the test scenarios. Blindness was confirmed and it fixed one problem — but a plain word-counter can still guess the CAS cell **42-48%** of the time when chance is **2.5%**.

- **G1 surface separability FAIL:** char-ngram TF-IDF **0.478125** (sd **0.053765**) and word-unigram **0.417187** (sd **0.030298**) against a bar of **≤ 0.10**; length control **0.032813 PASS**. This **reproduces the historical bag-of-words deadlock at 0.4851** that killed instruments v1 through v5b. (**Restated exactly 2026-08-19** — a previous revision carried the source document's own rounding, `0.4781` / `0.4172` / `0.0538` / `0.0303` / `0.0328`, which violates this sheet's rule 5.)
- **G2 vocabulary overlap PASS:** TKS **0.021749**, CAS **0.028179**, asymmetry ratio **1.2956** (**restated exactly 2026-08-19** from the rounded `0.0217` / `0.0282`). **G4 admissibility PASS** (640/640 unique, 0 duplicates, 40 labels). **G5 coverage PASS** (40/40 cells, 16-16 items/cell).
- Bank: **640 unique scenarios**, exactly **16 per cell** across all 40 cells, **160 per author**.

**Blindness is a PREREQUISITE, not a solution.** It fixed definition-**leakage**; it did not fix scenario **topicality** — the 40 concepts carry vocabulary even blind authors emit (spiritual items say sacred/contemplation, physical items say calloused/tangible, mental items say assumptions/systematically). **Reject-not-repair is binding (README R2/R3): do not patch a failed bank.** The G1 early-kill stopped the run before the labelling stage, so cost was authoring only.

**Do not cite:** the reported **G3 inter-rater 0.0** — labelling never ran, and the gate mis-fires on pre-labelling single-rater rows. It is an artifact, not an inter-rater failure.

Artifacts: `docs/working/gate2_closure/independent_bank/RESULT_TRACK_A_PILOT_G1_REJECTED.md`; `pilot_raw_gate_report.json`; `blindness_summary.json`; `docs/working/gate2_closure/INDEPENDENT_BANK_SPECIFICATION.md`.

### 7.7 Item-4 definition-anchored readout family — CLOSED, killed by a no-model check

An earlier attempt to show original TKS wording carries more meaning than compact CAS wording. **It was killed by a check that used no model at all:** matching each test item to whichever definition shares the most words reproduces the entire arm ranking, and **beats the actual language model by about 3×**.

Pure lexical overlap vs pythia-1b readout (chance **0.025**): A **0.4851** vs **0.1474**; B **0.4804** vs **0.1538**; D **0.1187** vs **0.0374**; E **0.0235** vs **0.0408**; F **0.0051** vs **0.0097**. **39 of 40 classes have a unique giveaway token.** Arm F is the proof: a permutation of Arm A's definitions — byte-identical vocabulary, identical **36.6%** overlap with the bank — but scrambled class assignment, and it scores at chance.

Successor arms, all negative: v2 pythia-1b criteria A2/A3/A5/A7 all failed (A-minus-D margin **0.1087**, CI **[0.0984, 0.1185]** against a **0.15** bar) → `NOT_LICENSED`; v3 composition → `VOID_SAME_DISEASE` (lexical control **0.0530**, not at chance); v4 masked → `NOT_LICENSED` (TKS margin **−0.0149**, permutation `p=0.901`, TKS not above chance); v5 multiplicative → `NOT_LICENSED` (both arms **1.0** — degenerate, margin **0.0**, `p=1.0`); v5b simspace → `VOID_DEGENERATE_METRIC` (**48.4%** of items excluded).

**Cause is benign and structural:** the TKS definitions and the bank glosses were authored by the same project about the same 40 concepts **17 days apart**. **The hard constraint: this bank CANNOT test the owner's question by ANY instrument**, because shared authorship guarantees a per-class giveaway token, and **no independently-authored 40E or F28 bank exists in the repo**. **The owner's actual question — does original TKS wording preserve more semantic signal than compact CAS — remains OPEN and UNTESTED. It is not refuted.** Any future item-4 design must report this lexical baseline alongside its headline and must beat it.

Artifacts: `docs/working/gate2_closure/item4_arms/LEXICAL_OVERLAP_DIAGNOSIS.md`; `item4_v2_results_pythia1b.json`; `item4_v3_results_composition.json`; `item4_v4_results_masked.json`; `item4_v5b_results_simspace.json`.

### 7.8 Global polarity steering — FALSIFIED (see Cap. 17)

Random norm-matched directions moved the refuse rate **more** than the CAS polarity direction (**0.30** vs **0.11**). One-sided, not the symmetric dose-response a causal axis predicts, with a fluency confound at high α. **A true negative, caught by the control rig.**

### 7.9 Component Atlas — three runs, zero labels stuck (see Section 6)

The single strongest scientific finding of that arc is **negative and specific**: at 2.8b the amplifier direction produced a large, highly significant, reproducible causal effect (`wilcoxon_pratt_p = 5.515e-05`, `behavioral_change_rate` **0.96875**) that size-matched random directions **beat by 2.7×** (`0.3660` vs `0.9766559642427914`). **Raw effect size at that layer is easy to obtain and worthless alone; selectivity is the whole game.** Rebuilding the null at 20B (orthogonalized, dose-matched, damage-guarded) did **not** rescue it — the targeted drop went **NEGATIVE (`-0.006726902197415563`)**.

### 7.10 Lacunarity as an injection detector — clean NEGATIVE (see Cap. 5)

Failed the decisive benign-append control in both forms; the faithful variant gave covert-vs-benign `p = 0.37` with **overt in the opposite direction** (`p = 1.3e-5`) and AUC **0.33**.

### 7.11 W0 prompt-injection licence — WITHDRAWN (see Cap. 27)

Hidden readout **89.6875%** lost to a character n-gram text control at **92.5-93.1%**. **Where a character control was run and lost, the claim was withdrawn.** That is why the missing 20B character arm (Cap. 1) is a live risk, not a formality.

### 7.12 The 20B F28 η→ε bridge MISSED its strict gate on the first readout — the pass followed an instrument swap

**Added 2026-08-19. This negative was missing from every prior revision of this sheet, which reported only the passing `+0.596413`.** It is material because it is an instance of this project's own named defect pattern — **changing a criterion or an instrument after an outcome is known** — the same shape as substituting a `107×` SNR guard for a missed absolute gate (Cap. 13, Cap. 30, §10 frontier 11).

The sequence, from `docs/working/cas_harness_original_closure_methodology_20260526.md`:

1. **First readout — nearest-centroid, `:410`.** Probe/readable delta **+0.1974**, **72/112** positive rows, `p = 0.001608` — and, verbatim, it *"miss[es] the original strict full-loop gate by about 0.0026."* Gold/readable on the same readout passed strongly: **+0.6601**, **93/112**. Raw CAS-symbol prefixes stayed near zero (**+0.0035**), matching the original null control.
2. **Diagnosis, `:411`.** When the probe predicted the Foundation correctly, probe/readable delta was **+0.6517**; when only the Drive was correct, **+0.7185**; when the Foundation was wrong, **−0.0752**. Conclusion recorded at the time: *"the bridge is not the bottleneck; the readout handoff/confidence filter is."*
3. **First rescue attempt — confidence filtering, `:412`. ALSO MISSED.** Centroid-margin filtering at `q25/q50/q75`: `q75` kept **28/112** rows, raised selected Foundation accuracy to **57.14%** and probe/readable delta to **+0.2775** — but sign-test `p` was **0.017849** rather than the required `≤ 0.01`. Verbatim: *"Simple margin filtering helps but is not enough by itself."*
4. **Second rescue — the readout swap, `:413`. PASSED.** *"Methodology correction: replacing nearest-centroid with the original balanced logistic linear-probe readout closes the 20B Step 11 bridge."* Result: **+0.596413**, **90/112**, sign-test `p = 3e-11`; gold-readable **+0.660065**, **93/112**; raw-symbol controls **+0.002524** probe raw, **+0.002186** gold raw. Foundation readout **86.8622%** held-out at layer 40; selected bridge-row Foundation accuracy **85.7143%**, Drive accuracy **93.75%**.

**Both sides of the honest read, and both must be given:**

- **In the swap's favour:** it was **disclosed in the source, not hidden**; the balanced-logistic readout is described as *"the original"* methodology, so this is a **restoration** rather than an invention; and no **threshold** was retuned — the gate stayed where it was and the instrument moved to meet it.
- **Against it:** the instrument was changed **after two failures on the same hypothesis were already known**, and the swap is the thing that converted a miss into the headline. Under this project's own discipline that is a **degree of freedom that was not pre-registered**, and it is not neutralised by having been disclosed.

**Binding reporting rule:** whenever `+0.596413` is quoted, `+0.1974` (`72/112`, `p = 0.001608`, miss by `~0.0026`) is quoted with it. **This is why Cap. 2 reads `REAL` + `PARTIAL` and not `VALIDATED`.**

### 7.13 Cross-cutting structural weaknesses

- **BRANCH SPLIT — no single checkout can reproduce one headline claim row end to end today.** Claims (spec sheets, summaries) live on HEAD (`codex/cascompass-legal-live-source`); raw 20B artifacts live on `master`; every non-160M model revision lives on `experiment/cas-probe-pythia`; the withdrawal tombstone lives on **unmerged commit `846ee041` that GitHub does not have**. **None of these is an ancestor of HEAD. The Gate 2 exit requirement "independently reproducible raw evidence" is NOT SATISFIED by the current tree.**
- **CONTROL COVERAGE IS THE WEAKEST LINK AT 20B.** No character-level n-gram control was ever run at 20B on either axis; on F28 at 20B **no text control at all** was run against the headline **86.862%**.
- **THE 20B MODEL REVISION IS UNRECOVERABLE.** `gpt_neox_20b_stage9_original_40e_capture_metadata_20260527.json` records `"model_revision": null`. **It must read `unavailable` and must never be filled in by looking up a plausible HuggingFace commit — that would be fabrication.**
- **ONE FIXTURE, ONE LANGUAGE.** All six model points used the same frozen English synthetic fixture, `input_sha256 3e4a1aca9f168a190116578b0b4fdb5bab633232ba06902039b233e589121250`, verified identical across all five stage manifests. Lab-independence holds only in the weak sense that six checkpoints came from three organisations; **fixture, protocol and labels are ours throughout.**
- **SINGLE SPLIT, SINGLE SEED.** Every F28 row: one fixed split (train **1344** / val **672** / test **2352**), one seed. No cross-validation, no cross-seed variation anywhere.
- **BLANKET SIX-MODEL WORDING IS OVERSTATED AND STILL LIVE** on `executive summary :12-17`, `spec sheet :28/:67/:83/:522`, `synopsis :24/:85`, `Amazon review brief :54`. **Gate 2 clause 3 ("remove blanket six-model wording") is UNMET — no live surface has been edited.**
- **COVERAGE IS A RECURRING, UNFIXED DEFECT** biasing every lens number optimistically: L1 exemplars **73%** (88/120), L1 real outputs **56%** (20/36), L2 presence **92%** (33/36), L2 wide **58%** (21/36), L2 wiring **69%** (25/36). Reasoning models drop the longest and hardest items, so **reported agreement is an upper bound in every case**.
- **TWO P0 SECURITY REGRESSIONS OPEN AND UNDEPLOYED** (RT-02, RT-05 — see Cap. 29). **The deployed system has ZERO withdrawal regression coverage.**
- **NO THIRD-PARTY CERTIFICATION.** No SOC 2, no ISO/IEC 42001, nothing. Evidence Packets **support** compliance documentation and do not by themselves satisfy any regulation.

### 7.14 Next-board prediction — a clean `NULL`, and conversations are STICKY

Added 2026-08-19. The lens was asked to predict the board of turn N+1 from turn N. It lost to the laziest possible rival and fell below its own permutation null.

- LOCO first-order Markov `board_acc` **0.5079** vs `persistence_acc` **0.5238** — **predicting "no change" beat the transition model.** Margin **−0.0162**, cluster-bootstrap `p5` **−0.0484** over `n_boot 300`.
- Within-conversation permutation null (`trials 200`, `seed 0`): mean **0.4761**, `p95` **0.5881**, **empirical `p` 0.4279**. **Shuffling labels inside a conversation did not destroy the apparent signal, because the apparent signal was autocorrelation, not prediction.**
- `nmi_bN_bNext` **0.2819** against `nmi_null_mean` **0.3264**, `nmi_p_empirical` **0.8109** — **the real mutual information is below its own null mean.**
- The board stayed the same across **33 of 63** transitions. `GATE3` and `GATE5` both **false**; report `VERDICT` field: `REJECTED`.

**The load-bearing read: this is a fact about conversation, not only about the lens.** Real assistant turns are persistent, so a next-turn task has almost nothing left to predict. That reframed the question toward the **transitions** — and the successor design then failed for a different reason (§7.16).

**Do not cite the four passing gates as partial support.** `GATE4` separation, `GATE6` user-move, `GATE7` turn-position and `GATE8` matched-taxonomy all passed **trivially**, because a predictor with no signal has no confound to catch.

Recover it as `git show aebe179f:docs/working/gate4_next_board/next_board_report_smoke.json`. The retired prereg `PREREG_NEXT_BOARD_V1.md` is left on disk unedited as the record.

### 7.15 The SDG multi-turn corpus — `WITHDRAWN` for two independent reasons, both found for $0

Added 2026-08-19. The project's own synthetic-dialog generator was proposed as a corpus with a built-in answer key. **Both kills were obtained by adversarial review plus a local computation, BEFORE any labelling call — no reader panel, no API spend.**

- **KILL 1 — the corpus is SURFACE-DETERMINED.** On the ground-truth task itself, LOCO folds grouped by conversation: **char TF-IDF(3,5) 1.0000, word unigram 1.0000, and RAW CHARACTER COUNT 1.0000.** The three classes have **disjoint** length distributions — `B0 30-97` chars, `B1` **exactly 104**, `B5 108-117` — so a **one-feature** classifier is perfect. **38 distinct assistant strings**, zero mapping to more than one board, so exact-string lookup is a **bijection** onto the answer key. Consequence, computed not argued: `PRIMARY_KILL_GATE_IS_SATISFIABLE_AT_ALL = false` — the gate requires `ra_acc − 1.0000 ≥ 0.05`, **impossible for any accuracy whatsoever.** *"An UNCOMPUTABLE control counts as a KILL, never as a pass."*
- **KILL 2 — MAPPING CIRCULARITY.** The turn-type → board answer key was authored **by reading the rendered template strings through the same rubric the reader panel is given.** `B1`'s entire prescribed class is **one byte-identical string** covering **90 of 228 turns**, whose wording is a near-verbatim cue for the B1 rubric's lead clause. The statistic therefore measures whether a panel applying rubric R to string S reproduces the label an author assigned to string S by applying rubric R. **It has NO INFORMATIVE RANGE: a pass is guaranteed by the authoring, a fail indicates reader noise only.**
- **The generator calls no model.** `_render_turn` selects from a fixed table and does `template.format(cas=...)` — no network request, no inference. **22 authored strings live** plus 6 unreachable dead constants; **7 distinct CAS expressions** in the whole generator; `PLAN` / `REFUSE` / `REFUSE_CLAIM` have one template each.

**Two disciplines worth carrying forward.** (1) **The phrase "KNOWN GROUND TRUTH" was UNEARNED and was deleted as an available verdict**, along with `CALIBRATED`; `gt_acc` was renamed `rubric_adherence_acc`. (2) **Preregistering a foregone kill is not a study** — the earlier design had said *"if the owner runs it anyway, it is to obtain that kill on the record"*, and the correction was to compute the kill locally for **$0** and make `--stage label` **refuse to spend money** while it fails.

**Do not read this as "template data is a bit weak".** It is not repairable by parameter choice — *"the template pool IS the artifact"* — and reviving the arm needs a different corpus **and** a key not derived from the rubric. **Not a relaxed bar.**

### 7.16 The board-CHANGE pilot — `VACUOUS`, and the six-code taxonomy produced TWO live categories

Added 2026-08-19. The successor to §7.14 spent its whole budget on the moments when the board changes. **Gate 0 failed on 6 of 19 checks with 1 uncomputable, so both claims are `VACUOUS` — never tested rather than tested and rejected — and no prediction number from the run may be cited.**

**The finding that outlives the run: the taxonomy does not fit natural conversation.** Consensus board labels over 157 complete cases: **`B0 115`, `B3 40`, `B2 1`, `B5 1`. `B1` and `B4` never reached consensus at all.** Raw reader marginals: `B0 315`, `B3 134`, `B5 13`, `B2 5`, `B4 3`, `B1 1`. **`B0` alone is 0.7325 of the consensus mass against a pre-registered ceiling of 0.40.** A six-category instrument that resolves to **two** categories on real model output is not miscalibrated; it is **mis-fitted**, and the record already contains the contrast that makes this specific: on the earlier corpus the same six codes spread evenly (`B1 20 / B2 9 / B3 13 / B4 16 / B5 18 / B0 18`, `b0_share` **0.1915**, kappa **0.5444**) — **because that corpus was built to exercise the codes.** Change the corpus to natural conversation and four of the six stop being used.

**Three Gate-0 failures are NOT pilot-size artefacts and would not be fixed by buying more conversations:**
- `fleiss_kappa_change` **0.2853** against a 0.35 floor, on **142** complete cases — landing inside the pre-declared `[0.2, 0.35)` `VACUOUS` band, above the 0.20 instrument-kill floor.
- `B0_share_of_consensus_board_labels` **0.7325** against **0.40**.
- `fleiss_kappa_user` **−0.0410** against 0.30 — **degenerate, not merely low.** Stratum N is continuers-only, so `P_e` is **0.9244** and the derived raw floor **0.9509** sits **above** the observed **0.9213**. **On this corpus that check could not have been met.**

The other failures — `raw_agreement_change` **0.7230** vs **0.7481**, `analysable_pairs` **138** vs a **240** floor, and the **uncomputable** `user_panel_positive_control_stratum_S` (`n=0` qualifying transitions) — are size- or construction-dependent.

**Recorded, and explicitly not evidence:** Claim 1 `change_f1` **0.2647** sits **below** the trivial `always_CHANGE` bar of **0.3171** and **below** the strongest surface arm `S3_length` at **0.4000**, with permutation `p` **0.6404** and MCC **0.0438** (bootstrap `p5` **−0.1846**). **Claim 2 `change_f1` is 0.0000 — the predictor never emitted `CHANGE` once in 138 pairs.** The kill statistic fires (`0.4 ≥ 0.2647`), **and the pre-registration forbids citing it because Gate 0 failed.** Cite none of it.

**The correction to a claim that is NOT in the record.** *"The recommendation on record is: do not fund the full run"* — **there is no such recommendation, and it must not be attributed to these artifacts.** §10.1 makes a Gate-0 failure a `VACUOUS` escape whose statistics may not be cited; **§15 forbids reading a pilot `VACUOUS` as a stop signal**; and the mechanical spend gate returned **`PROCEED — K_neutral = 72`** because `r_hat 0.1884` is above the `< 0.10` hard stop. **The three non-size failures above are what a funding decision should rest on. Say that instead.**

And **AMENDMENT A1 was logged BEFORE the run**, correcting an inherited misdiagnosis — an 800-token generation ceiling had been read as a generator-style confound when it was a **deterministic** ceiling that reasoning tokens exhaust, which an 8-conversation smoke exposed by producing **2 surviving conversations, both `qwen`**. A1 fixed it (median chars `deepseek 6188 / gemini 4906 / glm 4898 / qwen 14935`) **and flipped the confound's direction**: `GENERATOR_LENGTH_IMBALANCE_FLAG true` at ratio **3.0494**, with qwen now saturating the new budget.

### 7.17 WELD v1 — all four success criteria were true by construction

Added 2026-08-19. The first attempt to weld the five links into one machine **failed its own adversarial review**, and the failure was reported as a failure rather than dressed as a demo. The four defects share one shape: **not one of the four criteria could return `False`.**

1. **The matched control was an algebraic identity.** All 40 cells produce **distinct** prefixes (zero collisions; the label is embedded verbatim), and the true cell was **excluded from its own control pool**, so zero matches was a theorem — *"it would be 0/50, 0/500, 0/infinity."* **The pre-registered null `chance_rate_1_over_39 = 0.0256` is FALSE. The true null was exactly 0** — and the wrong baseline had been written into a machine-readable field for downstream consumers to inherit. **This is the single most important number in this subsection: never cite `0.0256`.**
2. **Axis N: the detector was handed the answer.** The loop scanned `f"{clean_expr} {inj.inverted}"`. **Scanning the perturbed object alone returns `clean=True`, `fired=[]`.** Axis N was the **only** criterion-(a)-passing axis, so the headline rested entirely on it.
3. **Axis W: the axis name was hardcoded** (`detected_axis = axis`), so criterion (a) evaluated `axis == axis`; `string_scan.fired_axes = []` confirms no detector fired. **This review step is what uncovered the shipped `_DOMAIN_RE` bug (§7.18).**
4. **The pipeline was not chained and criterion (b) was an involution identity.** The corrector received **ground truth**, so a total detection failure could not propagate; and the corrector **was** the injector, so `f(f(x)) == x`.

Also found: the string-plane scan covered **2 of 7** axes at runtime, **not the 5 of 7** claimed; and Stage 5 **could not run at all** as written (`ProbeShardConfig` has 9 further required fields with no defaults, so `--with-model` raised `TypeError` before any model loaded).

**The one genuine result, kept and elevated:** given **only** a perturbed pathway array with **no axis hint**, the Rust `cas_engine.InversionScanner` returns `fired_axes=['A']` and only `A`, at resistance **0.857143** = **6/7**. **It is the single honest detection in the loop, and it lives on the numeric plane, which cannot reach the epsilon-prefix joint.** WELD v2 (§Cap. 37) was built on exactly that one detection and nothing else — **and it DELETED criteria (c), (d1) and (d2) rather than repairing them**, because they lived on the realizer joint and could not be made falsifiable. **The reach of v2 is deliberately smaller than v1's. That trade — scope for falsifiability — is the lesson, not the loss.**

### 7.18 Axis W was DEAD in the Python belief gate — a six-axis scan wearing a seven-axis label

Added 2026-08-19. **This is the widest-reaching defect in this pass, and it is not confined to the experiment that found it.**

```
_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\^([PCEO])\b")        # BEFORE
```

`_` is a word character. In the drive-tagged literals this project actually emits there is **no word boundary** between the domain letter and `_{F5}`, so `\b` **never matched**.

```
BEFORE  _extract_domains('^8^E_{F5} -> ^6^C_{F5}')  ->  []
        axis_w_check(same) -> clean=True, reason='fewer than 2 domain markers'
AFTER   _extract_domains('^8^E_{F5} -> ^6^C_{F5}')  ->  ['E', 'C']
        axis_w_check(same) -> clean=False, 'precedence violated: E (rank 2) followed by C (rank 1)'
        axis_w_check('^8^C_{F5} -> ^6^E_{F5}') -> clean=True   (valid C->E descent stays clean)
```

**The failure mode is the dangerous kind: it returned `clean=True` with a plausible reason.** A domain-precedence violation — the `W` axis, one of the seven — could **never fire** on any drive-tagged expression anywhere in the repository. A caller reading `clean=True` had no way to tell "checked and clean" from "found nothing to check."

**BLAST RADIUS — stated as scope, not as measurement.** **Every consumer of `run_inversion_scan` has been silently running a scan short one axis whenever the expression carried a drive tag**: `belief_store.py`, `data/verifier.py`, and `api/routes/mode7.py`. Combined with the two known placeholder axes (`E` and `S` return `clean=True` with `placeholder=True` unconditionally), **the honest count on drive-tagged expressions was FOUR of seven, not seven and not five.** **No re-audit of prior scan verdicts has been performed** — that is §10 frontier 18, and until it is done, **no historical Python-side "clean scan" on a drive-tagged expression may be cited** (§5.2 item 29).

**Fix and evidence.** `_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\^([PCEO])(?![A-Za-z0-9])")` — `\b` with `_` permitted, rejecting only a following letter or digit (which would mean the marker is part of a longer token). **Seven regression tests added**, covering the drive-tagged violation, the drive-tagged valid descent, the register form `^3^P|A`, and a negative guard that `^Extra` is still not a domain marker. **Four of the seven fail against the old regex, so they are genuine regressions and not decoration.** `cas-native/tests/belief/`: **135 passed before, 142 after** (**21 → 28** in that file). The **24** unrelated failures elsewhere in `cas-native/tests/` (`test_trainer_v2.py`, `test_v2_evaluation.py`) were **confirmed pre-existing by re-running them with the change stashed.** Commit `f799fe98`; files `noetic-compass-scaffold/noetic-compass/cas-native/belief/inversion_gate.py` and `.../cas-native/tests/belief/test_inversion_gate.py`.

**The meta-lesson, and it is the reason this sits in §7 rather than in a commit log:** the bug was found by an **adversarial review of a build that was trying to claim a success**. A regex that silently returns "nothing to look at" is exactly the class of defect that no green test suite catches, because the suite had no drive-tagged case. **The scan said clean. The scan was not looking.**

### 7.19 Domain axis vs matched Tinbergen taxonomy — `INCONCLUSIVE BY DESIGN` (2026-08-22, pre-registered, $0)

The frontier-#1 lever was executed as pre-registered: v4 domain fixture (8 topics × 4 domains, 32 sentences), one capture pass on `pythia-160m-reserialized` (attested engine, CPU), and two probes on the SAME vectors — CAS domain labels vs Tinbergen's four questions under bijections frozen before capture. **The instrument cannot discriminate the hypothesis as constructed.** Nearest-centroid 4-way accuracy is invariant under any bijective class renaming (centroids permute with the labels, so every item's correctness is identical under every bijection). Observed: CAS and Tinbergen layer-mean **0.875 = 0.875**, best **1.0 = 1.0** (layer 2), identical per-layer accuracies at **all 12 layers** for BOTH bijections, Δ **0.0**, McNemar **p = 1.0** (0 discordant pairs) — all guaranteed by construction, not measured. Pre-registered criteria: C1 ✓ (CAS sanity — reproduces v4 domain decodability), C2 ✓, C3 ✗, C4 ✗. The prereg's literal verdict word was `DOMAIN_DOES_NOT_BEAT_GENERIC_ABSTRACTNESS`; **that wording is not citable** — the instrument could not have returned anything else, so the disposition is `INCONCLUSIVE BY DESIGN`: a negative about the instrument, not about the hypothesis. **Frontier #1 remains OPEN.** What would settle the lever: the Condition-3 blind-rater instrument (independent semantic annotation of the fixture into rival-taxonomy labels that cross-cut the domain partition), or a dual-labeled fixture bank. Artifacts: `docs/working/gate2_closure/cas_specificity/domain_vs_tinbergen_20260822/` (prereg `14ace6dd…`, runner `75cc73d9…`, fixture `0fb11c26…`, results `d6b0787d…`). Nothing was upgraded; the only positive content is the domain-decodability reproduction (layer-mean 0.875, best 1.0, shuffle 0.259, random-subspace 0.25).

**The open gate.** A policy draft exists that would make verified fallback its own separately versioned path: `Documents\Codex\2026-10-16\m1_h8_verified_fallback_policy_v0_1\POLICY_DRAFT.md`, sha256 `16773D53DDE1B257EA92F283627A07A1E86F211B239EAD76B5AC7988197303CA`, policy id `M1-H8-VERIFIED-FALLBACK` version `0.1`. It is **not frozen, not scored and not enabled**, and it has no owner signature. Its main rules: fall back only from a registered original copy of the same item version whose observed digest matches the authoritative expected digest; allow fallback in v0.1 only after `MISSING`, `CORRUPT` or `STALE`; one bounded attempt per copy; make the fallback visible in the answer and in the receipt and preserve the failed-primary touch; keep H8's rule unchanged and report the two outcomes separately; accept only 100% of the frozen matrix, 100% on positive and negative controls, complete valid receipts and zero safety failures, with no averaging away of a safety failure. It also names three declared failure-domain levels (`SYNTHETIC_SHARED_STORE`, `DECLARED_INDEPENDENT_DOMAINS`, `PRODUCTION_OPERATIONAL`) and requires every result to state its level; v5 is `SYNTHETIC_SHARED_STORE`.

- **What is licensed from this follow-up:** nothing beyond the synthetic matrix above. The useful finding is diagnostic: M1's §7.43 violations are ordered-copy-selection behavior against a strict rule, not lost or corrupted originals.
- **Not licensed:** any H8 pass; any durability or independent-failure-domain claim; any production claim; any statement about the frozen policy draft, which is a draft.
- **Design tension now on the record, for the owner:** strict H8 forbids an exact answer after a fault touch; verified fallback returns one when a healthy registered copy of the same version exists. The two cannot both hold. v0.1 keeps H8 as the governing rule and scores fallback separately, and a successful fallback still counts as an H8 failure.

### 7.46 M1 H8 verified creative reconstruction policy v0.2: the owner moved the line from "can a spare copy be checked" to "is the fault classified", and added a bounded, anchored, verifier-vetoed search for the unclassified case; FROZEN, nothing scored

This is a **policy definition**, not a behaviour result. No implementation exists, no row has been scored, and the claim ceiling is **NOTHING SCORED**.

**The change the owner made.** v0.1 (spec-sheet reference below) refused immediately on any fault it could not check a spare for: `MISSING` / `CORRUPT` / `STALE` allowed a verified fallback, and everything else — authorization failure, malformed metadata, conflicting manifests, unclassified timeouts — returned `UNKNOWN`. The owner pointed out that this line is a coincidence of which fault types happen to leave a readable twin, not a principle, and proposed instead a search: on a fault whose kind is not identified, scan the recorded memory, propose nearby readings within a creative radius, and verify before answering.

**What is frozen.** Policy id `M1-H8-VERIFIED-CREATIVE-RECONSTRUCTION`, version `0.2`, document sha256 `647ffc444a5911220909a88560a08bca276b5687c87a609729733df89c0386f9` (21,923 bytes, 146 lines, 9 top-level sections). Owner-authority record sha256 `4afda3bdb1ab89333252a7090373a7293eee5e42dd04b54aaf50f9d51b93b213`. It supersedes `M1-H8-VERIFIED-FALLBACK` v0.1, sha256 `16773D53DDE1B257EA92F283627A07A1E86F211B239EAD76B5AC7988197303CA`, which stays valid and is **not withdrawn**: it remains an accurate description of its own smaller idea.

| | What v0.2 adds | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | **Reclassification.** The line is *whether the fault is classified*, not whether a spare can be checked. Classified faults keep v0.1's rules; unclassified faults no longer stop at `UNKNOWN`. | 1 |
| ✅ | **Memory scan.** Read the breadcrumb's recorded fingerprint and the CAS-code capsule. Read-only; leaves no mark on the item. | 8 |
| ✅ | **Anchored proposal.** Candidates come from declared mutation operators over a declared anchor — the authoritative recorded fingerprint, or the last verified state of that version. Operator, seed and radius recorded per candidate. | 9 |
| ✅ | **Verifier veto.** Acceptance is an **exact match** against the authoritative fingerprint. Near matches, plausible readings and high-confidence proposals are all refused. There is no threshold below exactness. | 10 |
| ✅ | **Bounded widening driven by refusal.** Widening requires a matching refusal, is logged with its cause, and stops at a hard cap. No widening without a refusal. | 11 |
| ✅ | **No anchor, no reconstruction.** If the authoritative fingerprint is itself unavailable, the answer is `UNKNOWN` with reason `NO_ANCHOR`, and the policy **forbids** a wider radius as a substitute. This falls out of M1's own design, whose recall already returns `UNKNOWN` when neither the original's nor the capsule's digest passes. | 12 |
| ✅ | **Consequence routing.** The declared consequence class changes how hard the system tries, never how exact it must be. Symmetric cost may expand to the cap; asymmetric cost runs the near radius and refuses; an undeclared class behaves as asymmetric. | 15, 16, 17 |
| ✅ | **Receipt.** One query-bound, integrity-checkable receipt per recall carrying the fault class and the evidence that classified it, the anchor used and why, every candidate with operator, seed, radius and observed digest, every widening with its cause, and the routing decision. A reconstruction may never be presented as if it came from the preferred copy. | 18, 19 |

**The four frozen numbers.** The owner authorised the dispatch session to propose them ("propose them as defaults sign v0.2", 2026-10-16) and they are adopted into this freeze, changeable only by a dated amendment before the first scored row: initial radius **1** mutation unit; widening step **× 2** on a verifier refusal; hard cap **8** mutation units and at most **4** widening turns (worst case 15 candidates); asymmetric when the declared cost of a wrong answer is **≥ 20 ×** the cost of a refusal, or the consequence class is undeclared.

**Arms and controls, frozen before any run.** Arms: `A0_STRICT` (unchanged H8) and `A1_SPARE` (v0.1 fallback) as controls; `A2_KERNEL` is the arm under test. Four controls must **fail**, each matched so that only one mechanism differs: `C1_NO_VERIFIER` must return a plausible unverified answer as exact; `C2_UNANCHORED` must accept a wrong candidate or fail to reproduce an accepted one; `C3_NO_WIDENING` must fail to reach the recovery the kernel reaches; `C4_NO_CONSEQUENCE` must fail to refuse more on the asymmetric class.

**Safety floors, none averaged away:** zero wrong exact answers; zero plausible-unverified answers returned; zero unverified selections; zero mislabels of a reconstruction as an original; every refusal with a named reason; every candidate with operator, seed, radius and observed digest; every answer with a complete valid receipt; every returned unclassified-fault answer passed exact-match verification.

**The criterion.** `A2_KERNEL` clears all eight floors and recovers **strictly more** unclassified-fault items than `A0_STRICT` and **at least as many** as `A1_SPARE`; each of the four controls breaks its named floor; the radius widens at least once and every widening is reproducible from its logged seed and cause; and on the symmetric class the kernel refuses strictly fewer recoverable items than `A0_STRICT` while on the asymmetric class refusing no more than `A1_SPARE`. Acceptance requires 100% of planned rows executed, 100% of eligible positive rows exact, 100% of negative rows failing closed, 100% valid receipts and zero safety violations. **One wrong exact answer fails the whole result**, with no rescoring and no rescue run. Rates are reported separately and never combined into one score.

**Already recorded on this sheet and built into the design (section 6 of the document).** Three failure modes the policy is written against, all measured here: (1) **circular verification** — run R1-X0 reported "29 outputs, 0 problems" while three of its five exam files failed the receiving package's own checker, because its check recomputed the digest with the same algorithm that wrote the file's own checksum field (§7.44); (2) **randomness with no verifier** — "randomness as a proposer" earned keep in **0 of 8** tests, and in the language line the attempt read `VERIFIER_CANNOT_DISCRIMINATE`, separating 1 of 25 rows (§7.33, §7.34), which is why the creative path runs only where a fingerprint exists to check against; (3) **search that only goes down** — every search mechanism on this line descends, and the creative radius is the first attempt at breadth, with no prior evidence either way, stated rather than assumed.

- **What this licences:** nothing behavioural. It records a definition, four numbers and a test that can pass or fail honestly.
- **What it does not licence:** enabling creative reconstruction in HELM; changing H8; **any H8 pass at any point under any version of this policy**; scoring an implementation that was not frozen first; any AWS spend (an AWS pass needs its own owner line and cap, not covered by the HELM-R1 wave 1 cap); editing the frozen v5 package or the original M1 failure record.
- **Status.** FROZEN, not implemented, not enabled, not scored. The frozen v5 package and the original M1 failure (§7.43) and the v5 follow-up (§7.45) are untouched.
- **Artifacts (off-repo):** `Documents\Codex\2026-10-16\m1_h8_creative_reconstruction_v0_2\POLICY_v0_2_FROZEN.md` (sha256 `647ffc44…`), `OWNER_SIGNATURE_V0_2.json` (sha256 `4afda3bd…`), and beside them the working copy `POLICY_v0_2.md`, the freeze script `sign_policy_v0_2.py`, and the superseded `m1_h8_verified_fallback_policy_v0_1\POLICY_DRAFT.md` (`16773D53…`).

### 7.49 HELM end-to-end pipeline harness (`helm_end_to_end_loop.py`) and the conversational layer (`helm_chat.py`, `helm_memory.py`): `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`; the round-trip check is computed and never used, missing ingredients are filled with an invented 10, and the pipeline does not go through the gate, the repair loop or the D/W/P engine (2026-10-18, laptop, $0)

**What this is, plainly.** One Python file that takes a user's sentence and walks it through several parts in order: an English check, the valve, a recipe calculator, the cube store and a voice that answers in everyday English. A second layer (`helm_chat.py` with `helm_memory.py`) holds a conversation: it remembers facts the user states, tracks an inventory across turns, and tells statements apart from commands.

**Status: `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`.** It is built and it runs on its own tests. No frozen test with a control has scored it. The handoff calls it "WIRED & VERIFIED LIVE" (`MASTER_HANDOFF_20261018_CLAUDE.md` §0). This sheet does not, for the four reasons below, each read from the file.

**Four defects, each with its line (file `helm_end_to_end_loop.py`, committed blob sha256 `059b5a59b55bd654053bcb8c70253ebd390b61b08d29bfd37b3df9b0f9e4b17d`, last commit `a7dcc6b6`):**

1. **The round-trip check is computed and then ignored.** Lines 295-296 run `verify_cce_round_trip(user_english)` and store the answer in `result["cce_round_trip"]`. No later line reads it. A sentence that fails the round trip goes on exactly as one that passes. The project's own rule — a proposal must survive `parse(render(C)) == C` before it counts — is therefore not enforced here.
2. **Missing ingredients are filled with an invented number.** Line 421: `full_inputs = {ing: effective_inputs.get(ing, Decimal("10")) for ing in self.brain.ingredients}`. Every one of the 22 ingredients the user did not mention is set to 10 before the recipe is computed. Line 168 also sets any ingredient that is named without an amount to 10. That is an input the user never gave. It breaks the rule "an unknown face is reported as unknown and is never filled".
3. **The pipeline does not use the circuit that was built.** The file imports `helm_brain_22x40`, `tks_meta_valve_controller`, `helm_agentic_executor`, `cce` and the cube store. It imports none of `the_loop_v3/rpm_gate.py`, `repair_performer/`, `dwp_engine_v2/`, ASOM or Bias (searched in the file; the only "bias" is a valve feature named `operating_mode_bias`). So a turn never meets the real RPM gate, never opens a repair, and never descends. This contradicts the owner's direction that language rides the circuit path, and it is why queue row 15 (one live end-to-end trace) is still TODO.
4. **The recipe knowledge is hard-coded.** Flour and Water are the only "essential" reagents (lines 372-373, 408, 410), and the default limiting reagent is `"Flour"` (line 428). The "ungrounded" refusal is a list of four words (line 284: "quantum", "tuesday", "electron sandwich", "superstring").

**A safety note on the tool executor it calls** (`helm_agentic_executor.py`, sha256 `d4548b43b5af530d1e7c3d5f10ba1bd2b92dd90d7d3123086981cde270da9812`): `_execute_command` runs `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, …)` (line 384) behind a pattern filter. The cloud-dispatch tool is a dry-run receipt (line 412 comment "Simulation / dry-run dispatch receipt"); the file contains no `boto3`. The roadmap's "dispatch AWS cloud jobs" (§3.1) is therefore not what the code does.

### 7.50 HELM Phase 3 valve (`tks_meta_valve_controller.py`): `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`; a learned 5-weight logistic rule trained on the laptop (`LOCAL_CPU_DRYRUN_FAST`), **not** on AWS, sits in the deciding path; the owner ruled on 2026-10-18 that it be replaced by a plain written rule (2026-10-17/18, laptop, $0)

**What this is, plainly.** A gate in front of recipe execution. It does two things. First, if an essential ingredient is missing it shuts (`G-ABSENT`). That part is a plain rule. Second, it computes an "aperture" between 0 and 1 from five numbers about the request, and lets the request through only if its novelty score is at or below that aperture (`G-LIMIT` otherwise). That second part is **learned**: `sigmoid(w·x + b)` with five weights and one bias read from `tks_meta_valve_weights_v0_4.json` (`predict_dynamic_aperture`, used at `evaluate_proposal_flow` lines 121-124 and the admit/drop test at "Rule 2").

**Status: `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`.** The rule runs. No frozen test with a control has scored it.

**Where the weights came from — read from the weights file itself** (`tks_meta_valve_weights_v0_4.json`, committed blob sha256 `511ebe94360b108d1f6d90c897be0d061da3205b0ce1ef48c67caf5e67ff3ba5`):
- `"training_environment": "LOCAL_CPU_DRYRUN_FAST"`, `"training_samples": 2000`, `"final_mse": 0.09699948`.
- weights `-3.1026082`, `1.51951134`, `3.33129631`, `-1.06332357`, `0.52153234` on `novelty_entropy`, `source_credibility`, `prerequisite_ratio`, `normalized_radius`, `operating_mode_bias`; bias `-1.55750237`.
- validation: `"ungated_statistical_leaks": 83` of `"total_missing_prereq_rows": 250` (`33.2` %); `"gated_rpm_interlock_leaks": 0`.

**What the numbers mean.** Without the plain `G-ABSENT` rule, the learned part lets **83 of 250** requests with a missing ingredient through. With the plain rule, 0. So the safety comes from the written rule, not from the learning. The receipt `VALVE_ZERO_LEAK_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT.json` (side branch `helm/creativity-rpa-valve-v1`, commit `db39e8d6`) says the same: `"claim_ceiling": "ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED"`.

**A false claim, corrected here.** The roadmap's v0.4 row says "AWS GPU trained dynamic aperture weights" with status `SYNTHETIC_TRAINED` ✅ (`HELM_CAPABILITIES_ROADMAP_AND_DEVELOPMENTAL_STAGES.md` §3). The weights file says `LOCAL_CPU_DRYRUN_FAST`. No AWS job for the valve exists in the ledger (`AWS_COMBINED_ALLOCATION_HISTORY.jsonl`, searched). The trainer `train_tks_meta_valve.py` exists only on the side branch `helm/creativity-rpa-valve-v1`, not on the canonical branch.

**The "MUST REMEMBER valve" order.** The handoff, the L4 specification and the roadmap all quote *"MUST REMEMBER: Add, train, and test the VALVE SYSTEM (tks_meta_valve_controller) in Phase 3. This is CRITICAL."* No owner date and no owner source file for that sentence was found. Search scope: the canonical branch, `Documents\Codex\2026-10-16\` and `Documents\Codex\2026-10-18\` (`.md`, `.txt`, `.json`), and the project memory folder; the sentence appears only in the handoff, the L4 specification, the roadmap and a review note quoting them. Its owner source is recorded here as `unavailable`.

**The owner's ruling, 2026-10-18** (`C:\Users\wakil\Documents\Codex\2026-10-18\OWNER_APPROVALS_20261018.md`, item 3, "plain-rule valve"): *"the trained 5-weight logistic aperture in `tks_meta_valve_controller.py` is replaced by a written deterministic rule; learned parts stay out of the deciding path until they pass a frozen test."* That replacement (fix D) is **not done** in this commit; this section records the state before it.

- **Artifacts:** `tks_meta_valve_controller.py` (committed blob sha256 `7028b447efa82cfb4fe2edb87e94a520e47ceea85b3787d5e476c3ec1f2351c0`, last commit `7eb3511a`); weights file above; side-branch commits `fa924e17`, `db39e8d6`.
- **What this does not show.** That a learned valve helps. That anything was trained on AWS.

- **UPDATE 2026-10-18 (fix D, same day, above kept as recorded):** the learned aperture is out of the deciding path. `tks_meta_valve_controller.py` is now a written two-table rule (aperture from the missing ratio; noise level table), essentials passed in from the recipe's own prerequisite list, `G-ABSENT` kept, the weights file kept as history and never opened. ### 7.51 HELM stand-in brains `helm_brain_22x40.py` and `helm_brain_tks28.py`: `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`; demonstration brains, **not** the licensed brain; "22" is 22 baking ingredients and "40" is a parameter count, not CAS's 22 pathways or 40 states; no run id (2026-10-17, laptop, $0)

**What these are, plainly.** Two small recipe calculators. Each takes named amounts, applies one formula (a weighted power mean, the CES law `Y = [Σ cᵢ · max(0, xᵢ − aᵢ)^ρ]^(1/ρ)` in 40-digit Decimal), and names the ingredient that limits the output. They can also solve their weights exactly from example rows.

**Status: `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`** for both. Code runs. No run id, no frozen exam, no control, no recorded result.

**What the names mean, read from the code** (`helm_brain_22x40.py`, committed blob sha256 `ef8ccf6cd0242482e4b3b71bcd5d0e0ca286e96c7cad439b04f9a8418e4bb1b6`):
- **22** = 22 kitchen ingredients: `"Flour", "Water", "Sugar", "Egg", "Salt", "Yeast", "Milk", "Butter", "Cocoa", "Vanilla", "Honey", "Oil", "Oats", "Almonds", "Cinnamon", "Nutmeg", "Ginger", "BakingPowder", "BakingSoda", "Cornstarch", "LemonZest", "Molasses"`.
- **40** = 40 parameters: 22 weights + 1 curvature `ρ` + 17 thresholds (the file's own docstring: "Total = 22 + 1 + 17 = 40 parameters"). The 17 thresholds default to `0.0`.
- It is **not** CAS's 22 Capability Pathways and **not** CAS's 40 Cognitive States. No code in either file uses the real 22 pathways, 28 drives or 40 states.
- The file calls itself "Canonical". That word is the file's, not a status. It has no memory, no composition rule and no CAS structure.

`helm_brain_tks28.py` (side branch `helm/creativity-rpa-valve-v1` only, commits `d12e4078`, `347e03ef`; blob sha256 `fb1287f2adb24512e63e827da35af30ecf62869a2deaafa7dbd5430404d79d19`) is the same kind of CES calculator (`d40`, `d_pow`, `evaluate_recipe`, `solve_witness_weights`) over 28 inputs labelled as the 28 Foundations (4 planes × 7 archetypes). It is not on the canonical branch.

**Where the 22x40 brain is used.** It is the "Station S0" calculator inside `helm_end_to_end_loop.py` (§7.49), where the user's missing ingredients are filled with 10 before it runs.

**A misattribution, corrected here.** The roadmap (`HELM_CAPABILITIES_ROADMAP_AND_DEVELOPMENTAL_STAGES.md` §2.1 item 2) places "87.50% (448/512) … outperforming the AWS GPU Neural Net (60.74% / 311/512)" under the 22x40 brain. Those numbers are **RB-OH1's** (§7.52), a different program, and RB-OH1's own reading is `licensed: false`. The 22x40 brain has no score of its own.

**The owner's ruling, 2026-10-18** (`OWNER_APPROVALS_20261018.md` item 1): *"`helm_brain_22x40.py` / `helm_brain_tks28.py` are labeled demos / stand-ins."* The licensed brain is in §7.56. Fix G ("redeem 22x40": design the ledger universes on the real 40 states / 28 drives / 22 pathways) is approved and not started.

- **What this does not show.** Any score. Any link to CAS's real pathways, drives or states. That either file is HELM's brain.

- **UPDATE 2026-10-18 (fix C):** `helm_brain_22x40.py` now carries `DEMO_STANDIN` and `IS_CANONICAL = False`; the live loop no longer imports it. Station S0 is the licensed brain (§7.56), loaded by `helm_brain_canonical.py`. Record: `docs/working/traces/RESULTS_WIRE_RECIPE_BRAIN_20261018.md`.

### 7.52 HELM RB-OH1 (the substitution recipe head, five laptop parts plus AWS GPU job c32 for the tiny neural model): merged reading `HYBRID_ROUTING_EARNED` on the fresh worlds, `HYBRID_NO_BETTER` on the original worlds, sweep `SWEEP_CALIBRATION_FAILED`, `licensed: false` → `NOT LICENSED`; the "87.5% against 60.74%" numbers belong **here** (2026-10-17 PDT; c32 Tesla T4, RUN stage 36.817 s; charge `unavailable`)

The recipe side ran on the laptop in five parts. The tiny neural model (arm A7, "MLP (the tiny model)") ran once on an AWS GPU on the fresh worlds.

**Status: `NOT LICENSED`.** The merged reading itself says `"claim": {"ceiling": "SYNTHETIC_ONLY; no HELM claim; not adoption of SUB into CAS", "licensed": false}`. The words below are the frozen reader's own words, quoted, not status words of this sheet.

### 7.58 HELM DWP-T1 (Purpose / Wisdom / Power per reagent): the frozen rule's word is `TRIAD_EARNED_KEEP`; claim status `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, ceiling `SYNTHETIC_ONLY` — the answer keys use the same rules as the arms, so this shows the wiring works on planted data, **not** that real reagents carry a triad (2026-10-18 PDT, laptop MSI, 0 USD)

**Said plainly first.** The test checks whether a three-part label on each ingredient (Purpose, Wisdom, Power) can be wired into the recipe brain and read back correctly. It can. But the "right answers" were planted using the same definitions the arms use. So a pass was close to certain from the start (the builder wrote down about 85% before any code). It says the wiring works. It does **not** say any real ingredient, mind or model has such a triad. Nothing here is a HELM claim.

**Ordered by:** the owner's ruling "DWP-T1" (§7.59, item 3). Question source: `Documents/Codex/2026-10-18/EXPLORATION_PURPOSE_WISDOM_POWER_PER_REAGENT_v0.1.md` §4 (sha256 `729789d7350b502cb1e8713f2860001900aca130624df88c416e30fc6aa23cbe`).

**What was tested.** Each ingredient carries three faces. Each face has one of four stages on one scale: Rising `1/4`, Peak `1`, Waning `1/2`, Absent `0`. **Option A** shrinks each ingredient's amount by its triad. **Option B** puts one Purpose stage on the whole recipe (a door: Absent means the recipe may not run). Combining rules: `MIN` (`c = min(P, W, Pw)`, Balance Reading rule 1, `MANUSCRIPT.md:13600`) and `PRODUCT_BOOK` (`c = P × W × Pw × (1 − imbalance)`, `:13580`).

**Where the two face readings part ways (mixed_triads, report only).** Two rules can name the limiting face. *RPM-order reading:* the earliest face that is not at Peak, in the order Purpose, Wisdom, Power. *Smallest-value reading:* the face with the lowest stage value. They name a different face on **94 / 256** rows under A_MIN (36.7%) and on **105 / 256** rows under A_PROD (41.0%). The builder predicted 15–35% before code; the real share is higher. This test has no answer key for which reading is right.

**Imbalance factor.** The book's imbalance factor is underspecified (`MANUSCRIPT.md:13582`). The frozen reading is the range, `max − min`. It reproduces both worked examples in the book (`MANUSCRIPT.md:13585-13586`: (0.8, 0.8, 0.8) gives 0.512; (1.0, 0.6, 0.5) gives 0.15). Mean-absolute-deviation and max-minus-mean readings do not give 0.5 on the second example.

**What each option showed (one sentence each).** Option A found the hidden bottleneck: an ingredient with plenty of raw amount but one starved face, which today's single recipe and Option B both missed (they named the wrong ingredient on 512 / 512 starved rows). Option B is a door gate: it refused every recipe whose Purpose is Absent and scaled the whole yield for Rising and Waning, but it cannot say which ingredient or face is short.

**OPEN (not decided here; owner decisions).**
1. **Which face gets the blame:** the earliest face not at Peak in RPM order (Purpose, then Wisdom, then Power), or the face with the lowest value. On mixed_triads they disagree on 94 / 256 (A_MIN) and 105 / 256 (A_PROD) rows. `OPEN`.
2. **Which combining rule:** `MIN` or `PRODUCT_BOOK`. They give the same limiting ingredient and face on clean and starved data but different yields (336 / 512 starved rows, 255 / 256 mixed rows) and a different limiting ingredient on 52 / 256 mixed rows. `OPEN`.

### 7.60 HELM fix H, everyday English IN: a deterministic reader restates plain stock and recipe sentences in the checked form; the live loop runs them exactly like checked-form turns — `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`; MOOD_FACT_CLASH_CHECK `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, reported only (2026-10-18 PDT, laptop, 0 USD)

**Order.** Coordinator task H (owner direction "as fluid and as everyday English as possible", `OWNER_APPROVALS_20261018.md`). Platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14.0.

- **What it reads.** `helm_english_in.py`: stocks ("We have 50 flour, 30 sugar and 20 butter"; "there's 12 cups of flour" with the unit words kept), absences ("we're out of water", "no water", "the water is all gone", "there is 0 water"), the product asked about ("can we bake bread?", "how much bread can we make?", "what about bread?"), "bake a batch" (only the product already under discussion; else a question), and a witnessed batch ("we made 5 loaves from 10 flour and 8 water and ran out of flour" -> `witness_batch` -> the brain's own writer). Number, hedge and polarity words are the frozen ALIAS-WIDE lists (sha256 `d199611397d4d8ff5c215095d3424327917e4da9fcd5676e52cdd8c047a8b2e0`; equal to `lexicon_v2`'s, tested). Food words are the brain's 8 + 4 names plus a labeled plural table (OUR_CONVENTION).
- **No new facts.** Every reading is rendered by `language_v3/cce.py` and parsed back; used only if `parse(render(C)) == C`; then the loop checks it again as a checked-form sentence. Approximate, what-if, negated and relative amounts, unknown ingredients or products, missing numbers, unit switches, conversions, contradictions and incomplete batch reports get one plain question (22 codes) and **zero writes** (tested). A test checks that every amount read is a number the user said.
- **Same receipts.** Free English and checked form, turn by turn on a taught brain, give the same statuses, gate verdicts, write counts and brain receipts (test). Live trace tick 12 (free English) returns brain receipt `48ee0b4bac4d2567`, identical to checked-form tick 7.
- **Bug found and fixed.** A said-gone ingredient was glued back by the repair child from an older stored amount (HELM computed bread with water the user had just said was gone). Absences are now gated, round-tripped, written to the store and read back, and never re-glued.
- **Chat.** `helm_chat.py`'s side parser (and a second one in `helm_memory.AnaphoraResolver`) is removed; stock English goes through the loop, and the chat inventory mirrors the loop's verified stock. Every everyday reply goes through `helm_voice`; zero CAS tokens across a 13-turn chat test.
- **MOOD_FACT_CLASH_CHECK.** HELM does **not** understand sarcasm. One written rule: a 10-word positive mood list (not when negated) + a refusal / missing / "can't tell" receipt -> one plain question ("You said 'perfect', but there's no water on hand that I know of. Did you mean that?"). Facts unchanged (the reply without the mood word is an exact prefix of the reply with it; tested). `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, reported only.

Three tests were updated because they pinned the fix-C stopgap ("free English is refused"): loop test_14, loop test_18, voice chat test.

### 7.61 HELM DWP-T2 (does Wisdom only rise? three rules on planted worlds): the frozen rule's word is `C_EARNED_KEEP`; claim status `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, ceiling `SYNTHETIC_ONLY` — the worlds plant exactly the failures the rules name, so this measures what each rule costs and catches, **not** whether real know-how decays (2026-10-18 PDT, laptop MSI, 0 USD)

**Said plainly first.** Three ways to treat an ingredient's Wisdom were run side by side on made-up worlds. **A** never lets Wisdom go down. **B** lets it go down like Purpose and Power. **C** (the owner's choice) lets it go down only through a named event with evidence. On a world where Wisdom only rises, all three gave identical answers. On a world where Wisdom really decays, A kept the old value and gave wrong answers; B and C followed the truth at once. On a world where a saved Wisdom record was tampered on reload, A and B believed the tampered file; C caught every tamper. So C is kept for the next synthetic step. Nothing here says real minds lose know-how.

**Ordered by:** the owner's ruling "drops only by a named event with evidence [C]." and his note to re-examine Wisdom (§7.59 family; verbatim in `Documents/Codex/2026-10-18/OWNER_APPROVALS_20261018.md`); the build order relayed by the dispatch coordinator. ### 7.62 HELM triad adapter `helm_triad.py` (Purpose / Wisdom / Power around the canonical brain, Wisdom rule C, receipts): `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, `SYNTHETIC_ONLY`; default OFF; **0 learned parameters**; **not yet wired into the live loop** (2026-10-18 PDT, laptop MSI, 0 USD)

**Said plainly first.** A new wrapper lets each ingredient carry three faces on the owner's one scale. The lowest face sets how much of the ingredient counts. The licensed brain then answers exactly as before, on that reduced amount, and the answer also names the face to blame (the earliest weak one). A whole recipe with no Purpose gets "I can't tell yet — what is it for?" instead of a number. Wisdom can go down only through a named event with evidence. Every face write is read back and receipted. Nothing is learned. The sealed brain is not edited. With the switch off, nothing changes.

- **Rulings it obeys:** "Desire is Purpose"; one scale 1/4 / 1 / 1/2 / 0 for all three faces; "min"; "earliest"; Wisdom = C (`OWNER_APPROVALS_20261018.md`). Coordinator choices: Wisdom climbs 0 → 1/4 → 1/2 → 1; faces stored per ingredient.
- **What it is:** `TriadBrain(brain, table, enabled=False)` wraps `CanonicalRecipeBrain.evaluate()` and `witness()`; `TriadTable` holds the stated faces (sparse; each with a named source and evidence digest) and an append-only receipt log kept apart from the records. Effective amount `x_eff = min(P, W, Pw) × stock` (exact Fractions; every factor is exact in binary64). Recipe Purpose Absent → `UNDETERMINED`, gate `PURPOSE_ABSENT`, unsatisfied "the Purpose of Ω_X"; Rising / Waning → yield = η × Y_T. An Absent ingredient face → the brain's own G2 → `UNDETERMINED` with the face named. Reload: a record that fails its receipt → STORAGE_FAULT, value not taken, face UNKNOWN → `UNDETERMINED` until re-stated.

Default OFF identical **100 / 100**; triad ON at Peak identical to the brain **400 / 400**; planted starved face (decoy: the starved ingredient has the most raw stock) right ingredient **120 / 120** and right face **120 / 120**; receipts **52 / 52** read-backs passed, 4 bad writes refused with nothing written; 3-valued sums 80 + 1 + 1 = 82; Wisdom drop without event refused; with STORAGE_FAULT evidence accepted, with a receipt the table never wrote refused; UNEXPLAINED_YIELD and CORRECTION paths pass. **Learned parameters 0; stored values 3 in the test, ceiling 28** (8 × 3 + 4). Existing suites in the same worktree: end-to-end loop 18 OK, English-in 31 OK, voice 22 OK, chat nuance 5 passed.

On `a` the copy explained 22 rows for 320 new parameters, so the check refused it and nothing grew. No control fired. Everything else came out exactly as in RB-G8. **Coordinator decisions (instrument fixes, not research changes; verbatim in FROZEN.json):** (1) the job check must measure a grown copy's real explained rows, never the test fits' promise, keeping the ≥ 8-row rule and all guardrails; (2) drop the depth family (no arm reached depth 3 in RB-G8; depth growth is measured by wave 3's cascade exam, §7.66); (3) everything else frozen as RB-G8. **Which rows the fix counts (operator's reading, disclosed):** training rows newly explained by the grown copy, minus the same-capacity re-read — the count RB-G8's V8 read as 22. Not the scoring held-out panel: deciding growth on the panel that scores the arm would leak the score. The copy's validation and held-out changes are logged, reported only.

#### ERRATUM to 7.69 (2026-10-19 PDT): the arm called "round-robin" is round-robin PLUS a fixed table

**Said plainly first.** In the idle exam of wave 3 (job c37), one arm was written up as plain "round-robin" and scored 107 good. That label was wrong. That arm is round-robin plus a fixed look-up table that hands each kind of item the one faculty that can solve it. The real round-robin arm (no table) is the `-DRIVE_LOOP` arm, and it scored 31, the same as the drive loop. So the drive loop is neutral against true round-robin. It did NOT lose to round-robin 107.

- **What changes:** only the baseline label. The `DRIVE_LOOP` word stays `NEUTRAL`. No number changes. No reading, gate, instrument row or claim status changes. The original 7.69 text is left as written, and this erratum stands beside it.
- **What the code says (file `r1w3/drive_w3.py`, sha256 `79def344…`, byte-identical in the package and in the reader's copy):**
  - Lines 18-19: DRIVE_LOOP OFF is "Foundations in round-robin order ... the faculty by round-robin rotation (faculty index = Foundation index + tick, mod 7), no pull, no restart." This is the mechanism-free baseline.
  - Line 20: "REPORTED ONLY (not a switch arm): FIXED_TABLE_RR = round-robin Foundations with RB-I's fixed drive -> faculty table."
  - Lines 49-52 define the table (`RBI_TABLE`: F1 integration, F2 curiosity, F3 consolidate, F4 asking, F5 imagination, F6 verify, F7 pondering).
  - Line 159: `fac = (RBI_TABLE[f] if arm == "FIXED_TABLE_RR" else FACULTIES[(FOUNDATIONS.index(f) + t) % 7])`. The table is used only by `FIXED_TABLE_RR`.
  - Lines 56-58: `HOME` gives each kind its usual Foundation (DWP_CASCADE F7, ASOM_MISALIGNED_BIAS F6, LACUNA F4, NO_EVIDENCE F2). The table maps F7 to pondering, F6 to verify, F4 to asking, F2 to curiosity, which are the four faculties that can act on those kinds (`CAPABLE`, lines 53-54; check at line 90).
  - Counted by the writer of this erratum from the sealed exam file `x2_custody\exam\IDLE_X2.json` (sha256 `f883f8b0…`): 137 of the 180 items sit at their kind's home Foundation. So the table is right for those 137 by construction.
- **Corrected numbers (unchanged from `R1_W3_READING.json` sha256 `1cc7dba8…`, `numbers.X2_IDLE`; only the labels are corrected):**

| Arm | Correct label | GOOD | OPEN | WRONG | No progress | Redraws |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL (drive loop on) | drive loop | 31 | 149 | 0 | 207 | 147 |
| -DRIVE_LOOP | TRUE round-robin (no table), the mechanism-free baseline | 31 | 149 | 0 | 207 | 0 |
| FIXED_TABLE_RR | round-robin PLUS the fixed table (reported only, not a switch arm) | 107 | 73 | 0 | 131 | 0 |

- **Corrected reading:** the drive loop is `NEUTRAL` against true round-robin (31 vs 31). The 107 is what a hand-made fixed table gets on this exam, where 137 of 180 items are filed at the home Foundation the table was written for. It is NOT a round-robin score. The text in 7.69 that says "round-robin 107" and the Open line "The drive loop lost to plain round-robin on idle (31 vs 107)" should be read as "the drive loop was level with true round-robin (31 vs 31); the fixed-table arm scored 107." The same wrong label sits in `RUN_RESULT_R1W3_C37.md` (table row "FIXED_TABLE_RR (round-robin)" and the bullet "Plain round-robin did far better: 107 good against 31") and in the 2026-10-19 Change Log row for 7.69 ("round-robin 107"). Those originals are not edited.

**Said plainly first.** The owner asked for one more growth run on a world where gaps come in several kinds at once, so a refusal counter should lose to curiosity, and said to stop the line if it fails. RB-G10 built three new worlds. Each Omega needed two different kinds of capacity (a second route and a leak term, or a recipe slot and a leak term). Wrong growth used up a budget of N = planted kinds + 1 units. The strongest cheap rival was added: a refusal counter that guesses the kind from the residual pattern and uses the same real-rows check. The test did not happen. Even the pre-sized brain (ORACLE) scored exactly the same as the start brain on all three new worlds, so the frozen answer-key rule found no valid world. The recipe engine cannot fit this two-kind law: the second route can only be found on rows the leak has not touched, and the leak can only be fitted once the right route is in place. The status word is `INCONCLUSIVE`, not a FAIL. The owner's stop rule names a FAIL, so what happens next is the owner's decision.

### 7.73 HELM U3-T1 self-scan by the Unity Eye (368 synthetic copies, 17 arms, 6 laptop parts, $0): status word `SELF_SCAN_EARNED_KEEP` and whisper word `WHISPER_EARNED_KEEP` by the frozen rule; claim status `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`, ceiling `SYNTHETIC_ONLY` — the faults were planted knowing what the scan checks (2026-10-19 PDT, laptop MSI, 0 USD)

**Said plainly first.** U3 gives HELM a read-only look at itself. The Unity Eye runs a Mind scan (what the brain was taught, tested on, slipped on, never used) and a Body scan (do saved records still read back, do the sealed brain files match their seal, do old store answers still re-derive, is the gap ledger in order). It never writes; a problem becomes a proposal. It reports in plain English, and every fact sentence must point to a record. Owner ruling: the Eye REPORTS AND WHISPERS. A whisper is a typed nudge to the brain's presentation policy through the normal gate; it never writes a cell or changes a dial, and the brain may ignore it. On 368 built copies of HELM's state, the full scan found and named all 176 planted body faults with their records, raised 0 false alarms, changed 0 answers, and all 20,768 fact sentences traced back to records. A fixed after-every-write checklist found 16 (only faults present at write time). A random spot-check found 148 (its chance value is about 153). **The four parts.** S — 128 real sentences (32 per stratum: quantity, absence, question, other), each alone on an empty brain, then "What do we have on hand?". R-ASIS — 64 real recipes told as "We made 1 {N} from {lines} and ran out of {ingredient}.", a pantry from a second real recipe, then "How much {N} can we make?". R-REBOUND — the same on real 2- and 3-ingredient recipes with the brain's fixed recipe shape renamed per recipe (REBIND, word tables swapped and restored). F — 192 restart worlds (save with HELM's own serializers, one fault, reload with HELM's own loaders, "Hi again.", one idle window, the probe): T1 tail lost, T2 torn record, E1 mojibake, E2a byte-order mark, E2b CRLF (benign), D1 duplicate line, S1 stale rollback, C1 clock reset (benign), 16 each, + 64 clean.

**Keys.** Written rules only, three values (a key, ASK, UNDETERMINED = not scored). Key A by the builder; key B by a separate agent session that read only the written rule and never HELM's code; items where they disagree become UNDETERMINED; agreement must be at least 90% (I2; practice 204 of 205).

**Rivals.** Always-ask (B-ASK), a reckless keyword reader (B-KEYCALC), an echo (B-ECHO), HELM with the reader or the voice off, the Eye report-only, wave 4's after-write checklist, and a plain file checksum kept outside the state (WATCHDOG, same Gate and receiver as the Eye).

**Marks (the designer's PROPOSED thresholds, unchanged):** S at most 2 WRONG, at least 4 RIGHT more than always-ask, fewer WRONG than the keyword reader, at most 2 non-plain replies, Eye quiet; R at most 2 WRONG; R-REBOUND RIGHT on 3/4 of answerable items (read only with at least 16 answerable items, A-XR-5); F no false alarm on 64 clean worlds, every caught damage the answer uses is held. Hard gates: receipts, the Eye writes nothing, the voice changes no answer, replay identical, no key reaches the host, no network, the brain folder unchanged, baselines on the same inputs.

So HELM learns one requirement per real recipe and cannot answer P2 on a 2- or 3-ingredient recipe. Fixing it would need invented amounts, which the mapping forbids.
- **The designed pairing rule almost never gives an answerable question (A-XR-5).** B = the next-ranked recipe sharing at least one ingredient: 4 of 400 and 0 of 400 items got an ANSWER key on two test rank strings (no seed); 208 and 211 of 400 had some B holding all of A's ingredients. - **Practice dry run (21 units from the sealed extract, all exit 0, 48.66 s, one worker):** on 128 practice sentences FULL wrote 7 wrong facts (e.g. "no water on hand" for "Tom pulled Mary out of the water"; "two eggs" for "Mix the flour with two eggs"); the keyword reader wrote 2. ### 7.83 RB-W1 wide brain BUILT, NOT TESTED on a sealed exam; claim status `ENGINEERED-NOT-VALIDATED`; licensed brain unchanged (2026-10-19 PDT, laptop, 0 USD)

**Said plainly first.** Owner order (verbatim): "WIDEN THE BRAIN" (0 USD to build). The recipe-shape survey (`Documents\Codex\2026-10-19\recipe_shape_survey_v1\SURVEY.md`) found the licensed brain fits 1 of 13,686 real recipes: 8 ingredient words, 4 fixed shapes of 2-3 ingredients, no thirds, no units. RB-W1 is a SEPARATE, wider brain beside it, behind a switch `WIDE_BRAIN` that is OFF by default. It learns with the same rule (one witnessed batch, one ingredient ran out first: a := stock / amount made, exact) and answers with the same rule (yield = min x_i / a_i; the smallest ratio is the Limiting Reagent). It is not curiosity growth: a recipe is added only when an admitted witnessed batch introduces it, and a coefficient only from a batch where that ingredient alone ran out. Everything else stays `UNDETERMINED` and the brain asks.

Round trip `parse(say(q)) == q` checked on 2,112 fractions (denominators 1-32) |

- **The defect (`CONT3_DIAGNOSIS.md`).** `lm_t4/stations.py`, `TaskBThinker.s5`, line 520: the asking crossing (faculty F4 naming the absent support slots of a recipe at station S5) was recorded with label `ATTEMPTED` (open now) and key `CREATED` (expected to be answered later) for BOTH brains of a Task B draw.
